English: Camel Post
A rough post marked only by tethering poles and a few makeshift tents, where camels and traders gather at the edges of the wild.
Merchants Tent
A sturdy canvas tent, the first place for itinerant merchants to barter and rest, drawing passing caravans in search of supplies.
Pack Animal Shelter
Simple timber-framed lean-tos and mud-brick pens for camels, mules, and horses, offering better care for valuable beasts of burden.
Walled Pavilion
A low-walled pavilion surrounds the encampment, providing security and a central rallying point for traders and nomads alike.
Market Room
A semi-permanent wooden structure serves as a bustling market, drawing distant traders and boosting the local economy.
Trade Hall
A grand timbered hall for negotiations, feasts, and the exchange of contracts, anchoring the caravanserais reputation as a mercantile hub.
Camel Stable
Stone-built stables allow for breeding and care of large herds of camels, vital for long-distance trade and nomadic war hosts.
Merchants House
Permanent residences for wealthy merchants, with secure vaults and private courtyards, attracting long-term investment and population.
Storage Pavilion
Expansive brick warehouses under watchful guards, ensuring the safe deposit of goods for caravans and increasing trade capacity.
Iranian Grand Caravanserai
A sprawling fortified caravanserai of baked brick and stone: a true center of commerce, diplomacy, and nomadic unity on the Silk Road.
